after.instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 10 mL final-volume basis, charge N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol: 1.26 mmol (0.126 M final); add the declared solvent to 10 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation.
Prepare Stream B: connect H2 to the assigned MFC at 1 mL/min at STP on the declared STP basis (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar; 22.414 L/mol); no liquid stock is prepared.
Assemble only the inventory-assigned process graph and verify every equipment ID and connection against the final diagram.
Prime each liquid line with its declared solvent using its assigned pump until the outlet is bubble-free; do not introduce reactive feeds during priming.
Pressure-test with compatible inert fluid to the approved operating setpoint of 21 bar and verify stable pressure before reagents.
Purge the gas path with the inventory-declared nitrogen source, verify oxygen removal by the laboratory-approved method, then isolate nitrogen before hydrogen admission.
Verify the declared non-return/check valve is installed in the hydrogen feed in the correct flow direction.
Verify the gas-liquid separator off-gas is connected to the declared safe vent before hydrogen admission.
Confirm grounded ventilation is active and ignition sources are excluded.
Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Stop hydrogen, purge residual gas, and depressurize in a defined sequence.
Start liquid feeds at the canonical setpoints. Admit gas only after liquid flow, temperature, pressure, purge, and vent checks are stable.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 90 min, based on three nominal liquid-volume turnovers. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present.

After measured steady state, collect a timed fraction over at least 30 min as an initial sampling interval; record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume. Extend collection if needed for the analytical method.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.

before.answer: N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol (DMAOL; MW 239.32 g/mol) was prepared as a 3.8 wt% solution in methanol. The solution density is assumed to be 0.792 g/mL (approximately 0.126 M DMAOL). A 200 mL charge was contacted with hydrogen over 0.5 g of 7 wt% Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 catalyst in a stirred batch reactor at 60 °C and 21 bar for 5 h. Conversion to 3-azetidinol was 38.1%.

Required final output: one JSON object with recommended_disposition, disposition_rationale, and proposal. The proposal must be a JSON object, not a JSON-encoded string. The proposal uses these fields:

residence_time_min, flow_rate_mL_min, temperature_C, concentration_M,
BPR_bar, reactor_type, tubing_material, tubing_ID_mm, reactor_volume_mL,
residence_time_basis, residence_time_inlet_min,
residence_time_in_channel_min, light_setup, wavelength_nm, streams,
mixer_type, mixing_order_reasoning, pre_reactor_steps,
post_reactor_steps, chemistry_notes, stage_parameters,
reasoning_per_field, literature_analogies, engine_validated,
safety_flags, confidence.

Each stream is an object with stream_label, pump_role, contents, solvent,
phase, flow_rate_mL_min, concentration_M, molar_equiv, gas_flow_sccm, and
gas_flow_actual_mL_min where applicable. Distinguish inlet/STP gas flow from
pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow. Ensure reactor_volume_mL is consistent
with flow and residence time. State assumptions rather than inventing missing
facts.

recommended_disposition must be exactly EXECUTE, SCREEN, or BLOCK. Use BLOCK
when the hard constraints make a safe design physically or operationally
impossible. Use SCREEN for a feasible first experiment that still requires
experimental validation. Use EXECUTE only for a directly executable design
supported by sufficient evidence.

controls.description: Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Leak- and pressure-test the assembled system before reagent introduction.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Purge and verify oxygen removal before admitting hydrogen.
Use declared non-return or check-valve protection on the hydrogen feed.
Route separator off-gas to a declared safe vent.
Use grounded ventilation and remove ignition sources.
Stop hydrogen, purge residual gas, and depressurize in a defined sequence.

validation_experiments: Run compatible blank solvent at Q=0.1 mL/min, T=60.0 C, and BPR=21 bar for at least 10 min; record flow, temperature, pressure, leaks, and blockage indicators.

Introduce a compatible nonreactive tracer at Q=0.1 mL/min and measure its outlet response after correcting for external tubing delay. Report the measured mean, dispersion and liquid holdup separately from the calculated 2.72727 min index (inlet/STP apparent residence time); do not require agreement with an STP turnover index.
Execute the canonical operating procedure once and report conversion, isolated yield, selectivity, pressure trace, temperature trace, and any phase or blockage observations.
Perform the laboratory-approved inert leak and purge qualification using the exact final gas path; do not introduce hydrogen until every safety control is signed off.
